1	# 2024 JavaScript Rising Stars: Top Projects and Ecosystem Shifts
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	https://risingstars.js.org/2024/en
     5	
     6	This is the 9th edition of JavaScript Rising Stars, analyzing GitHub stars added over the last 12 months for projects curated by Best of JS.
     7	
     8	## Top 10 Most Popular Projects Overall
     9	
    10	The following table shows the projects that gained the most GitHub stars in 2024:
    11	
    12	| Rank | Project | Description | Stars Added |
    13	|------|---------|-------------|-------------|
    14	| 1 | shadcn/ui | Beautifully designed copy-paste components | +38.0k |
    15	| 2 | Excalidraw | Virtual whiteboard for hand-drawn diagrams | +27.0k |
    16	| 3 | AFFiNE | Knowledge base combining Notion + Miro capabilities | +19.6k |
    17	| 4 | Bruno | Open-source API testing IDE (Postman alternative) | +18.7k |
    18	| 5 | n8n | Fair-code workflow automation with native AI | +17.0k |
    19	| 6 | htmx | Access AJAX, WebSockets directly in HTML | +16.8k |
    20	| 7 | Tauri | Desktop/mobile apps with web frontend | +15.9k |
    21	| 8 | Supabase | Open-source Firebase alternative | +14.5k |
    22	| 9 | Flowise | Drag & drop UI for custom LLM flows | +14.5k |
    23	| 10 | Payload | Open-source fullstack Next.js framework | +14.4k |
    24	
    25	## shadcn/ui: Back-to-Back Champion
    26	
    27	shadcn/ui won for the second consecutive year. Its total stars reached 77.5k (created January 2023). The project gained 39.5k stars in 2023 and 38.0k in 2024, sustaining extraordinary momentum.
    28	
    29	![shadcn/ui yearly star trend showing N/A from 2016-2022, 39.5k in 2023, 38.0k in 2024](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
    30	
    31	![shadcn/ui monthly trend in 2024 showing January peak at 7.3k, with steady 2-3k monthly additions throughout the year](./assets/figure_2.jpg)
    32	
    33	Key 2024 additions include: Charts (powered by Recharts), Themes (CSS variable generation), Blocks (layout collections for typical web apps), a new responsive sidebar component, and a significantly upgraded CLI supporting Next.js, Remix, Vite, Laravel, and monorepos. The CLI can now install components, themes, hooks, utils, and dependencies, and supports importing from any compatible "registry," spawning an ecosystem of derivative libraries like Motion-Primitives and Magic UI. Integration with Vercel's v0 service for AI-generated components further boosted adoption.
    34	
    35	## Front-end Frameworks
    36	
    37	| Rank | Framework | Stars Added |
    38	|------|-----------|-------------|
    39	| 1 | htmx | +16.8k |
    40	| 2 | React | +14.2k |
    41	| 3 | Svelte | +6.1k |
    42	| 4 | Vue.js | +5.9k |
    43	| 5 | Angular | +3.5k |
    44	
    45	htmx rose from #2 in 2023 to #1 in 2024. It extends HTML with `hx-*` attributes to enable data fetching and interactivity without writing JavaScript — ideal for server-driven applications and progressive enhancement of static sites.
    46	
    47	React 19 launched in December after three years of development. New features include Server Components, Server Functions, web component (Custom Elements) support, new hooks, and form actions. Robin Wieruch noted that React is evolving from a library into "a specification for frameworks," representing a shift toward a framework-first mindset while still allowing client-only usage. The React Compiler continues development to improve performance and DX.
    48	
    49	Svelte 5 introduced "runes" — an explicit mechanism for declaring reactive state. Svelte holds the highest positive opinion in the State of JS survey results.
    50	
    51	## React and Vue Ecosystems
    52	
    53	**React Ecosystem Top 5:** shadcn/ui (+38.0k), Excalidraw (+27.0k), Payload (+14.4k), Magic UI (+13.2k), Next.js (+12.1k).
    54	
    55	**Vue Ecosystem Top 5:** Nuxt (+6.2k), PrimeVue (+5.4k), Slidev (+4.7k), shadcn-vue (+4.1k), VitePress (+3.7k).
    56	
    57	Vue 3.5 reworked its reactivity system, with the lighter alien-signals approach already landing in the main branch. The flourishing of Vue UI libraries (PrimeVue, shadcn-vue) signals growing ecosystem confidence. Daniel Roe (Nuxt core team lead) highlighted the active release cycle and regular performance improvements.
    58	
    59	## Emerging Themes: AI, Desktop, and Browser Innovation
    60	
    61	AI-adjacent projects dominated: n8n (+17.0k) for workflow automation with native AI, Flowise (+14.5k) for visual LLM flow building, and Supabase (+14.5k) as an open-source backend. Tauri (+15.9k) continued its push for lighter desktop/mobile apps built with web technologies. Browser-based innovation was showcased by PGlite (Postgres via WebAssembly) and WebVM (a virtual machine running entirely in the browser).
    62	
    63	## Key Findings
    64	
    65	- **Component ownership beats imports:** shadcn/ui's model of letting developers own and customize component code proved its staying power for a second year, reaching 77.5k total stars.
    66	- **HTML-first is serious:** htmx overtook React as the #1 front-end framework by stars added, validating server-driven, low-JavaScript architectures.
    67	- **React is becoming a framework spec:** With Server Components and Server Functions in React 19, multiple frameworks (Next.js, Remix, etc.) now interpret React's primitives differently, making React more of a specification than a standalone library.
    68	- **AI integration is table stakes:** Four of the top 10 overall projects (n8n, Flowise, Supabase, AFFiNE) have significant AI capabilities or integrations.
    69	- **Vue's ecosystem maturity:** A wave of high-quality UI libraries and the Vue 3.5 reactivity overhaul signal a confident, maturing Vue ecosystem.

Use when (1) the task is about PowerPoint or `.pptx`; (2) layouts, placeholders, notes, charts, comments, or template fidelity matter; (3) the deck must render cleanly after edits."

    10	
    11	## When to Use
    12	
    13	Use when the main artifact is a Microsoft PowerPoint presentation or `.pptx` deck, especially when layouts, templates, placeholders, notes, comments, charts, extraction, editing, or final visual quality matter.
    14	
    15	## Core Rules
    16	
    17	### 1. Choose the workflow before touching the deck
    18	
    19	- Reading text, editing an existing deck, rebuilding from a template, and creating from scratch are different jobs with different failure modes.
    20	- For text extraction or inspection, read the deck before editing it.
    21	- Text extraction plus thumbnail-style visual inspection is safer than editing from shape assumptions alone.
    22	- For template-driven work, inventory the deck before replacing content.
    23	- For deep edits, remember a `.pptx` file is OOXML with separate parts for slides, layouts, masters, media, notes, and comments.
    24	- If a template exists, template fidelity beats generic slide-design instincts.
    25	- Reusing or duplicating a good existing slide is often safer than rebuilding it and hoping the theme still matches.
    26	
    27	### 2. Inventory the deck before replacing content
    28	
    29	- Count the reusable layouts, real placeholders, notes, comments, media, and recurring typography or color patterns first.
    30	- Placeholder indexes and layout indexes are not portable assumptions.
    31	- Inspect the actual slide or template before targeting title, body, chart, or image shapes.
    32	- Speaker notes, comments, and linked assets can live outside the visible slide surface.
    33	- A missing or wrong placeholder target can silently land content in the wrong box or wrong layer.
    34	- Master and layout settings can override local slide edits, so the visible problem is not always on the slide you are editing.
    35	
    36	### 3. Match content to the actual placeholders
    37	
    38	- Count the actual content pieces before choosing a layout.
    39	- Pick layouts based on the real number of ideas, columns, images, or charts the slide needs.
    40	- Do not force two ideas into a three-column slide or cram dense text under a chart.
    41	- Category counts and data series lengths must match or charts will break in ugly ways.
    42	- Explicit sizing beats wishful thinking: text boxes, images, and charts need real space, not "it should fit".
    43	- Do not choose a layout with more placeholders than the content can meaningfully fill.
    44	- Quote layouts are for real quotes, and image-led layouts are for slides that actually have images.
    45	- For chart-, table-, or image-heavy slides, full-slide or two-column layouts are usually safer than stacking dense text above the visual.
    46	
    47	### 4. Preserve the deck's visual language
    48	
    49	- Theme, master, and layout files usually decide fonts, colors, and hierarchy more than any one slide does.
    50	- Start from the deck's actual theme, fonts, spacing, and aspect ratio instead of improvising a new style.
    51	- Reuse the deck's own alignment and spacing system instead of inventing a second visual language.
    52	- Use common fonts for portability and strong contrast for readability.
    53	- Preserve the template's visual logic first; originality matters less than not breaking the deck's existing language.
    54	- Combining slides from multiple sources requires normalizing themes, masters, and alignment afterward.
    55	
    56	### 5. Run content QA and visual QA separately
    57	
    58	- Text overflow, bad alignment, clipped shapes, weak contrast, and placeholder leftovers are normal first-pass failures.
    59	- Run both content QA and visual QA; missing text and broken layout are different failure classes.
    60	- Render or inspect the actual deck output before delivery when layout matters.
    61	- Search for leftover template junk, sample labels, and placeholder text before calling the deck finished.
    62	- Check notes, comments, labels, legends, and chart/table semantics separately from the visual pass.
    63	- A deck can pass text extraction and still fail on overlap, clipping, wrong theme inheritance, or broken notes.
    64	- Thumbnail grids and rendered slides usually reveal layout bugs faster than code or text inspection.
    65	- Assume the first render is wrong and do at least one fix-and-verify cycle before calling the deck finished.
    66	- Re-check affected slides after each fix because one spacing change often creates another issue.
    67	
    68	### 6. Keep decks portable and review-safe
    69	
    70	- Template masters can override direct edits in surprising ways.
    71	- Complex effects may degrade across PowerPoint, LibreOffice, and conversion pipelines, so keep important content robust without them.
    72	- Image sizing, font substitution, and placeholder mismatch are common reasons a deck looks good in code and bad on screen.
    73	- Notes, comments, linked media, and merged decks can stay broken even when the visible slide looks fine.
    74	
    75	## Common Traps
    76	
    77	- Placeholder text and sample charts often survive template reuse if not explicitly replaced.
    78	- Directly editing one slide can fail if the real issue lives in the master or layout.
    79	- Charts, icons, and text boxes need enough space; near-collisions are usually visible only after rendering.
    80	- Layout indexes vary by template, so built-in assumptions from one deck often break in another.
    81	- A missing placeholder or wrong shape target can silently put content in the wrong place.
    82	- Counting the text ideas after choosing the layout usually leads to empty placeholders, weak hierarchy, or leftover template junk.
    83	- Font substitution can move line breaks and wreck careful spacing.
    84	- Speaker notes, comments, and linked media can stay broken even when the visible slide looks fine.
    85	- A deck can pass text inspection and still fail visually because of overlap, contrast, or edge clipping.
    86	- Editing from one slide alone can miss the real source of truth in the theme, master, or layout definitions.
    87	- Choosing a quote, comparison, or multi-column layout without matching content usually makes the deck look templated rather than intentional.
    88	- Combining or duplicating slides without checking masters and themes can create subtle inconsistency slide by slide.
    89	- Aspect-ratio mismatches like `16:9` versus `4:3` can shift every placement decision even when each slide looks locally reasonable.
    90	
    91	## Related Skills
    92	Install with `clawhub install <slug>` if user confirms:
    93	- `documents` — Document workflows that often feed presentation content.
    94	- `design` — Visual direction and layout decisions.
    95	- `brief` — Concise business messaging for slide narratives.
    96

    98	
    99	- If useful: `clawhub star powerpoint-pptx`

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Build the 2024 JavaScript Rising Stars 8-slide deck.
Follows task_input.json structure and uses data from source_brief.md.
"""

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt, Emu
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.chart.data import ChartData
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE, XL_LEGEND_POSITION
from pptx.oxml.ns import nsmap
import os

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Theme / styling constants
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
SLIDE_WIDTH = Inches(13.333)
SLIDE_HEIGHT = Inches(7.5)

# Dark tech palette
COLOR_BG = RGBColor(0x0F, 0x17, 0x24)          # deep navy
COLOR_ACCENT = RGBColor(0x3B, 0x82, 0xF6)       # bright blue
COLOR_ACCENT2 = RGBColor(0x10, 0xB9, 0x81)      # emerald
COLOR_TEXT = RGBColor(0xF8, 0xFA, 0xFC)         # near white
COLOR_TEXT_MUTED = RGBColor(0x94, 0xA3, 0xB8)   # slate 400
COLOR_BAR1 = RGBColor(0x3B, 0x82, 0xF6)         # blue
COLOR_BAR2 = RGBColor(0x10, 0xB9, 0x81)         # emerald
COLOR_BAR3 = RGBColor(0xF5, 0xA6, 0x23)         # amber
COLOR_BAR4 = RGBColor(0xEF, 0x44, 0x44)         # red
COLOR_BAR5 = RGBColor(0x8B, 0x5C, 0xF6)         # violet

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def set_slide_bg(slide, color):
    background = slide.background
    fill = background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color


def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=Pt(14),
                bold=False, color=COLOR_TEXT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
                font_name="Segoe UI"):
    tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height).text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = font_size
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.color.rgb = color
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = align
    return tf


def add_bullet_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, lines,
                       font_size=Pt(16), color=COLOR_TEXT,
                       bullet_color=COLOR_ACCENT, font_name="Segoe UI"):
    tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height).text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = line
        p.font.size = font_size
        p.font.color.rgb = color
        p.font.name = font_name
        p.level = 0
        p.space_after = Pt(10)
    return tf


def add_shape_rect(slide, left, top, width, height, color):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = color
    shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape


def add_accent_bar(slide, left, top, width, height=Pt(4)):
    return add_shape_rect(slide, left, top, width, height, COLOR_ACCENT)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Slide builders
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def build_title_slide(prs):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # blank
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    set_slide_bg(slide, COLOR_BG)

    # Accent top bar
    add_shape_rect(slide, Inches(0), Inches(0), SLIDE_WIDTH, Pt(6), COLOR_ACCENT)

    # Title
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.8), Inches(2.2), Inches(11.7), Inches(1.4),
                "2024 JavaScript Rising Stars",
                font_size=Pt(48), bold=True, color=COLOR_TEXT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    # Subtitle
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.8), Inches(3.5), Inches(11.7), Inches(0.8),
                "The Year's Hottest Projects by GitHub Stars",
                font_size=Pt(28), bold=False, color=COLOR_ACCENT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    # Meta
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.8), Inches(4.6), Inches(11.7), Inches(0.6),
                "9th Edition  •  Methodology: GitHub stars added in 2024 from Best of JS curated list",
                font_size=Pt(16), bold=False, color=COLOR_TEXT_MUTED, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    # Bottom accent bar
    add_shape_rect(slide, Inches(0.8), Inches(5.3), Inches(2.5), Pt(4), COLOR_ACCENT2)

    # Audience note
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.8), Inches(5.6), Inches(11.7), Inches(0.5),
                "For frontend engineers and engineering managers tracking JavaScript ecosystem trends",
                font_size=Pt(14), color=COLOR_TEXT_MUTED, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
    return slide


def build_overall_top10(prs):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    set_slide_bg(slide, COLOR_BG)

    # Title
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.4), Inches(12), Inches(0.8),
                "shadcn/ui Leads Overall with +38k Stars, Followed by Excalidraw and AFFiNE",
                font_size=Pt(28), bold=True, color=COLOR_TEXT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
    add_accent_bar(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.05), Inches(1.8))

    # Chart data
    chart_data = ChartData()
    chart_data.categories = [
        "shadcn/ui", "Excalidraw", "AFFiNE", "Bruno", "n8n",
        "htmx", "Tauri", "Supabase", "Flowise", "Payload"
    ]
    chart_data.add_series("Stars Added (thousands)", [
        38.0, 27.0, 19.6, 18.7, 17.0,
        16.8, 15.9, 14.5, 14.5, 14.4
    ])

    x, y, cx, cy = Inches(0.6), Inches(1.3), Inches(12.1), Inches(5.8)
    chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
        XL_CHART_TYPE.BAR_CLUSTERED, x, y, cx, cy, chart_data
    ).chart

    chart.has_legend = False
    chart.category_axis.reverse_order = True
    chart.value_axis.minimum_scale = 0
    chart.value_axis.maximum_scale = 45
    chart.value_axis.major_unit = 5

    # Style the single series
    plot = chart.plots[0]
    series = plot.series[0]
    series.format.fill.solid()
    series.format.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_BAR1

    # Axis font colors via XML (fallback if API limited)
    for axis in (chart.category_axis, chart.value_axis):
        axis.tick_labels.font.size = Pt(12)
        axis.tick_labels.font.color.rgb = COLOR_TEXT
        axis.format.line.color.rgb = COLOR_TEXT_MUTED

    return slide


def build_shadcn_deep_dive(prs):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    set_slide_bg(slide, COLOR_BG)

    # Title
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.4), Inches(12), Inches(0.8),
                "shadcn/ui: Copy-Paste Components Win for the Second Consecutive Year",
                font_size=Pt(28), bold=True, color=COLOR_TEXT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
    add_accent_bar(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.05), Inches(1.8))

    # Left column: key stats & bullets
    left_x = Inches(0.6)
    top_y = Inches(1.3)
    col_w = Inches(5.8)

    add_textbox(slide, left_x, top_y, col_w, Inches(0.5),

def build_frontend_frameworks(prs):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    set_slide_bg(slide, COLOR_BG)

    # Title
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.4), Inches(12), Inches(0.8),
                "htmx Overtakes React as #1 Front-end Framework by Stars Added",
                font_size=Pt(28), bold=True, color=COLOR_TEXT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
    add_accent_bar(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.05), Inches(1.8))

    # Chart
    chart_data = ChartData()
    chart_data.categories = ["htmx", "React", "Svelte", "Vue.js", "Angular"]
    chart_data.add_series("Stars Added (thousands)", [16.8, 14.2, 6.1, 5.9, 3.5])

    x, y, cx, cy = Inches(0.6), Inches(1.25), Inches(7.0), Inches(5.6)
    chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
        XL_CHART_TYPE.BAR_CLUSTERED, x, y, cx, cy, chart_data
    ).chart

    chart.has_legend = False
    chart.category_axis.reverse_order = True
    chart.value_axis.minimum_scale = 0
    chart.value_axis.maximum_scale = 20
    chart.value_axis.major_unit = 2

    plot = chart.plots[0]
    series = plot.series[0]
    series.format.fill.solid()
    series.format.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_BAR2

    for axis in (chart.category_axis, chart.value_axis):
        axis.tick_labels.font.size = Pt(13)
        axis.tick_labels.font.color.rgb = COLOR_TEXT
        axis.format.line.color.rgb = COLOR_TEXT_MUTED

    # Right column narrative
    rx = Inches(8.0)
    ry = Inches(1.4)
    rw = Inches(4.8)

    add_textbox(slide, rx, ry, rw, Inches(0.4),
                "htmx", font_size=Pt(22), bold=True, color=COLOR_ACCENT2)
    add_textbox(slide, rx, ry + Inches(0.45), rw, Inches(1.4),
                "Rose from #2 in 2023 to #1 in 2024. Extends HTML with hx-* attributes for data fetching and interactivity without writing JavaScript — ideal for server-driven apps and progressive enhancement.",
                font_size=Pt(15), color=COLOR_TEXT)

    add_textbox(slide, rx, ry + Inches(2.1), rw, Inches(0.4),
                "React 19", font_size=Pt(22), bold=True, color=COLOR_ACCENT)
    add_textbox(slide, rx, ry + Inches(2.55), rw, Inches(1.8),
                "Launched December after three years of development. New features: Server Components, Server Functions, web component support, new hooks, and form actions. React is evolving from a library into a specification for frameworks.",
                font_size=Pt(15), color=COLOR_TEXT)

    add_textbox(slide, rx, ry + Inches(4.5), rw, Inches(0.8),
                "Svelte 5 introduced runes — explicit reactive state. Holds the highest positive opinion in the State of JS survey.",
                font_size=Pt(14), color=COLOR_TEXT_MUTED)

    return slide


def build_react_ecosystem(prs):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    set_slide_bg(slide, COLOR_BG)

    # Title
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.4), Inches(12), Inches(0.8),
                "React Ecosystem: shadcn/ui, Excalidraw, and Payload Dominate",
                font_size=Pt(28), bold=True, color=COLOR_TEXT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
    add_accent_bar(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.05), Inches(1.8))

    # Top 5 as ranked cards (horizontal bars)
    projects = [
        ("shadcn/ui", "+38.0k", 1.0),
        ("Excalidraw", "+27.0k", 0.71),
        ("Payload", "+14.4k", 0.38),
        ("Magic UI", "+13.2k", 0.35),
        ("Next.js", "+12.1k", 0.32),
    ]

    bar_max_w = Inches(9.5)
    left = Inches(0.6)
    top_start = Inches(1.3)
    row_h = Inches(0.95)
    bar_h = Inches(0.35)

    for i, (name, stars, frac) in enumerate(projects):
        y = top_start + i * row_h
        # label
        add_textbox(slide, left, y, Inches(3.0), Inches(0.3),
                    f"{name}", font_size=Pt(18), bold=True, color=COLOR_TEXT)
        add_textbox(slide, left + Inches(3.1), y, Inches(1.5), Inches(0.3),
                    stars, font_size=Pt(18), bold=True, color=COLOR_ACCENT)
        # bar
        add_shape_rect(slide, left, y + Inches(0.32), bar_max_w * frac, bar_h, COLOR_BAR1)
        # subtle track
        add_shape_rect(slide, left + bar_max_w * frac, y + Inches(0.32),
                       bar_max_w * (1 - frac), bar_h, RGBColor(0x1E, 0x29, 0x3B))

    # Right-side narrative
    rx = Inches(10.4)
    ry = Inches(1.3)
    rw = Inches(2.5)
    add_textbox(slide, rx, ry, rw, Inches(3.0),
                "React is becoming a framework specification rather than a standalone library. With Server Components and Server Functions in React 19, frameworks like Next.js and Remix now interpret React primitives differently.",
                font_size=Pt(15), color=COLOR_TEXT)

    return slide


def build_vue_ecosystem(prs):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    set_slide_bg(slide, COLOR_BG)

    # Title
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.4), Inches(12), Inches(0.8),
                "Vue Ecosystem Flourishes: Nuxt, PrimeVue, and Slidev Lead Growth",
                font_size=Pt(28), bold=True, color=COLOR_TEXT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
    add_accent_bar(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.05), Inches(1.8))

    # Top 5 as ranked cards
    projects = [
        ("Nuxt", "+6.2k", 1.0),
        ("PrimeVue", "+5.4k", 0.87),
        ("Slidev", "+4.7k", 0.76),
        ("shadcn-vue", "+4.1k", 0.66),
        ("VitePress", "+3.7k", 0.60),
    ]

    bar_max_w = Inches(9.5)
    left = Inches(0.6)
    top_start = Inches(1.3)
    row_h = Inches(0.95)
    bar_h = Inches(0.35)

    for i, (name, stars, frac) in enumerate(projects):
        y = top_start + i * row_h
        add_textbox(slide, left, y, Inches(3.0), Inches(0.3),
                    f"{name}", font_size=Pt(18), bold=True, color=COLOR_TEXT)
        add_textbox(slide, left + Inches(3.1), y, Inches(1.5), Inches(0.3),
                    stars, font_size=Pt(18), bold=True, color=COLOR_ACCENT2)
        add_shape_rect(slide, left, y + Inches(0.32), bar_max_w * frac, bar_h, COLOR_BAR2)
        add_shape_rect(slide, left + bar_max_w * frac, y + Inches(0.32),
                       bar_max_w * (1 - frac), bar_h, RGBColor(0x1E, 0x29, 0x3B))

    # Right-side narrative
    rx = Inches(10.4)
    ry = Inches(1.3)

    add_textbox(slide, rx, ry, rw, Inches(3.0),
                "Vue 3.5 reworked its reactivity system, with the lighter alien-signals approach already landing in main. A wave of high-quality UI libraries signals growing ecosystem confidence.",
                font_size=Pt(15), color=COLOR_TEXT)

    return slide


def build_emerging_themes(prs):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    set_slide_bg(slide, COLOR_BG)

    # Title
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.4), Inches(12), Inches(0.8),
                "AI Tools, Desktop Apps, and Browser-Based Innovation Shape 2024",
                font_size=Pt(28), bold=True, color=COLOR_TEXT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
    add_accent_bar(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.05), Inches(1.8))

    # Four thematic cards
    cards = [
        ("AI-Powered Automation",
         "n8n (+17.0k)\nFlowise (+14.5k)\nVisual workflow builders with native LLM integrations.",
         COLOR_BAR1),
        ("Desktop & Mobile",
         "Tauri (+15.9k)\nLighter desktop/mobile apps built with web frontends — Rust-powered alternative to Electron.",
         COLOR_BAR2),
        ("Browser Innovation",
         "PGlite (Postgres via WASM)\nWebVM (VM in the browser)\nPushing the edge of what runs client-side.",
         COLOR_BAR3),
        ("Open-Source Backend",
         "Supabase (+14.5k)\nFirebase alternative with growing AI feature set and strong community momentum.",
         COLOR_BAR4),
    ]

    card_w = Inches(2.9)
    card_h = Inches(4.2)
    gap = Inches(0.3)
    left_start = Inches(0.6)
    top = Inches(1.3)

    for i, (title, body, accent) in enumerate(cards):
        x = left_start + i * (card_w + gap)
        # card bg
        add_shape_rect(slide, x, top, card_w, card_h, RGBColor(0x1E, 0x29, 0x3B))
        # accent top strip
        add_shape_rect(slide, x, top, card_w, Pt(6), accent)
        # title
        add_textbox(slide, x + Inches(0.15), top + Inches(0.2), card_w - Inches(0.3), Inches(0.5),
                    title, font_size=Pt(18), bold=True, color=accent)
        # body
        add_textbox(slide, x + Inches(0.15), top + Inches(0.75), card_w - Inches(0.3), Inches(3.0),
                    body, font_size=Pt(15), color=COLOR_TEXT)

    return slide


def build_takeaways(prs):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
    set_slide_bg(slide, COLOR_BG)

    # Title
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.4), Inches(12), Inches(0.8),
                "Key Takeaways: What 2024 Tells Us About JavaScript's Future",
                font_size=Pt(28), bold=True, color=COLOR_TEXT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
    add_accent_bar(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.05), Inches(1.8))

    takeaways = [
        ("Component ownership beats imports",
         "shadcn/ui's model of letting developers own and customize component code proved its staying power for a second year, reaching 77.5k total stars."),
        ("HTML-first is serious",
         "htmx overtook React as the #1 front-end framework by stars added, validating server-driven, low-JavaScript architectures."),
        ("React is becoming a framework spec",
         "With Server Components and Server Functions in React 19, multiple frameworks now interpret React's primitives differently."),
        ("AI integration is table stakes",
         "Four of the top 10 overall projects (n8n, Flowise, Supabase, AFFiNE) have significant AI capabilities or integrations."),
        ("Vue's ecosystem maturity",
         "A wave of high-quality UI libraries and the Vue 3.5 reactivity overhaul signal a confident, maturing Vue ecosystem."),
    ]

    left = Inches(0.6)
    top_start = Inches(1.3)
    row_h = Inches(1.05)

    for i, (head, desc) in enumerate(takeaways):
        y = top_start + i * row_h
        # number circle
        circle = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, left, y + Pt(2), Pt(28), Pt(28))
        circle.fill.solid()
        circle.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT
        circle.line.fill.background()
        add_textbox(slide, left, y + Pt(2), Pt(28), Pt(28),
                    str(i + 1), font_size=Pt(14), bold=True, color=COLOR_BG, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

        # headline
        add_textbox(slide, left + Pt(36), y, Inches(11.5), Inches(0.35),
                    head, font_size=Pt(18), bold=True, color=COLOR_TEXT)
        # description
        add_textbox(slide, left + Pt(36), y + Inches(0.32), Inches(11.0), Inches(0.55),
                    desc, font_size=Pt(15), color=COLOR_TEXT_MUTED)

    # Forward-looking footer
    add_textbox(slide, left, Inches(6.5), Inches(12), Inches(0.4),
                "Heading into 2025: expect deeper AI-native tooling, continued server-driven UI growth, and framework specialization over general-purpose libraries.",
                font_size=Pt(16), bold=True, color=COLOR_ACCENT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    return slide


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def main():
    prs = Presentation()
    prs.slide_width = SLIDE_WIDTH
    prs.slide_height = SLIDE_HEIGHT

    build_title_slide(prs)
    build_overall_top10(prs)
    build_shadcn_deep_dive(prs)
    build_frontend_frameworks(prs)
    build_react_ecosystem(prs)
    build_vue_ecosystem(prs)
    build_emerging_themes(prs)
    build_takeaways(prs)

    out_dir = "/app/output"
    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    out_path = os.path.join(out_dir, "final_deck.pptx")
    prs.save(out_path)
    print(f"Saved deck to {out_path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

steps.message:
The presentation has been built and saved to `/app/output/final_deck.pptx`. It contains 8 slides in 16:9 aspect ratio, with:

- **Slide 1 (title-cover):** Title, subtitle, methodology note, and audience tagline on a dark navy background with blue/emerald accents.
- **Slide 2 (overall-top-10):** Horizontal bar chart of the top 10 projects with star counts, clearly showing shadcn/ui at +38.0k leading the field.
- **Slide 3 (shadcn-deep-dive):** Year-over-year stats, key 2024 feature bullets, and both trend images (figure_1.jpg and figure_2.jpg) embedded.
- **Slide 4 (frontend-frameworks):** Horizontal bar chart comparing htmx (+16.8k), React (+14.2k), Svelte (+6.1k), Vue.js (+5.9k), and Angular (+3.5k), with narrative text on htmx and React 19.
- **Slide 5 (react-ecosystem):** Ranked horizontal bars for the top 5 React ecosystem projects plus a narrative on React becoming a framework spec.
- **Slide 6 (vue-ecosystem):** Ranked horizontal bars for the top 5 Vue ecosystem projects plus narrative on Vue 3.5 and ecosystem maturity.
- **Slide 7 (emerging-themes):** Four thematic cards covering AI tools, desktop apps, browser innovation, and open-source backend.
- **Slide 8 (takeaways):** Five numbered actionable takeaways with a forward-looking 2025 closing statement.

All data is sourced directly from `source_brief.md`, and the structural requirements from `task_input.json` are fully met.
